evidence.V1: Front and three-quarter read clearly as a wall torch (flame, cup, handle, back plate), but the flame is a rounded faceted cone that reads more like a gem or ice-cream scoop than fire, and the top view is an unreadable lump.
evidence.V2: Clear big/medium/small: flame + handle as the big masses, cup and back plate medium, iron ring and the gold drip lip at the cup rim as small accents.
evidence.V3: Handle is a plain straight tapered cylinder and the plate a flat box; the flame has no tongues or lean, so only partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Back plate, cup rim and ring carry visible soft chamfers that catch light, but the flame is hard-faceted with sharp creases, so edge treatment is inconsistent across parts.
evidence.V5: Close_flame_studio shows irregular faceted patches and pinched creases across the flame shell (not a clean designed facet pattern); handle, cup and plate are clean.
evidence.V6: Flame in two orange values plus gold lip, wood-brown handle, ink iron; colourways (teal, violet) swap only the flame hue - disciplined.
evidence.V7: 576 tris vs small target 600 (ceiling 1500): at target.
evidence.V8: Palette (gold, ink, wood) and plate/cup chamfers match the kit, but the hard-faceted flame breaks the smooth weighted-normal look.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a wall light: anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch off, back-centre origin, PointLight note, MeshPart white with vertex colours.

artifacts: Patchy faceting / pinched creases across the flame shell in close_flame_studio
Ring sits loosely around the handle with a small visible gap (0.012 studs)
top_fixes: Rebuild the flame as a smooth fused shell with 2-3 flicking tongues and a slight lean so it reads as fire at 64 px
Seat the iron ring snugly on the handle and give the arm a clearer link to the plate
Add a subtle taper/flare or a wrap band on the handle to break the plain cylinder
